title: How I got here
lead: I started at a hotel front desk, not in a code editor. Technology came later, out of the problems and processes I saw every day. Today that combination lets me understand both the operation and the tools that keep it running.

steps.title: Hospitality
steps.line: I started working in a hotel, then moved through corporate reception at Dorna Sports during the MotoGP seasons, high-occupancy hotels and, today, the daily operation of an apart-hotel.

steps.title: Operations
steps.line: Reservations, availability, rooms, billing, guest service, channels and pricing. I have worked daily with PMS such as Opera and Avalon and with OTAs such as Booking.com and Expedia.

steps.title: Technology
steps.line: Studying Web Application Development is what took me from using software to understanding how it is built. Since then I have built my own products, integrated APIs and maintained real applications in production.

items.title: Real operational context
items.text: I know the day to day of a property: priorities, incidents, guests, reservations, rooms, channels and coordination across teams.

items.title: Connection between operations and product
items.text: I understand what hotel users need and I can pass it on to an engineering or product team with context, priorities and real use cases.

items.title: Ability to build
items.text: Beyond understanding the problem, I can prototype solutions, work with APIs and build and maintain web products in production.
